summary: Cross-project contracts, phase 4: the feature becomes visible and shippable. The loop composes a contracts block into the session prompt when (and only when) this repo declares dependencies — naming each one, stating the vendored contract is authoritative, forbidding guessing, forbidding edits to the vendored copy, and naming the refresh command. Every stack-profile verify template seeds the consumer check, positioned immediately after the `cd` so it runs ahead of any stack-specific fail-open. docs/CONTRACTS.md is the full reference, registered scaffold-class and in the default profile; QUALITY_GATES, CONTAINERIZATION, EXECUTION_MODES, META_SPEC and README cross-reference it.
decision_memo: foundry-meta/KICKOFF-phasekit-v070-contracts.md phase 4; awareness rationale per DESIGN-cross-project-contracts.md ownership split ('a mount nobody is told about goes unread')
suggested_commit_message: v0.7.0 phase 4: session awareness, stack seeding, docs
reviewer_notes: Prompt composition runs AFTER light-mode composition, so both apply: a light task is exactly as capable of guessing a field name as a standard one. Pinned by test.

Prompt composition fails open — a malformed contracts.yaml adds nothing to the prompt rather than killing the session before it starts. The gate is where a bad declaration must be loud, and failing open here keeps the session reaching that gate, where the error is reported properly.
A repo declaring nothing (or declaring zero entries) gets the v0.6.6 prompt byte for byte, asserted by equality rather than by absence of a substring.

The seeded check moved from the tail of each template to immediately after the `cd`. Caught in end-to-end smoke: the python-uv template fail-opens when there is no pyproject.toml yet, so a tail-positioned check never ran on a young repo. A contract violation is not something to skip because the stack's own preconditions are not met. A test now pins that nothing exits between the `cd` and the check, in all five templates.

Five near-identical seeded blocks are the one real duplication this release adds. Consolidating them is not available — they are templates seeded once into project-owned files that then diverge by design — so the invariant is enforced by a test asserting all five blocks are byte-identical, the same pin-not-abstraction approach used for the '/contracts' path across the bash/python boundary.

docs/CONTRACTS.md states the CI boundary explicitly (a fork's green CI badge proves conformance but not freshness) so it is read rather than discovered. Doc assertions run against whitespace-collapsed prose, so they pin what the doc says rather than where its lines wrap.

docs/META_SPEC.md's standalone goal already anticipated this design in the abstract ('the thing that decides whether it is required must live in the project repo'); it now points at v0.7.0 as the worked example.
